root.claim: Exact multiplication of two $n$-bit integers runs in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time on one deterministic fixed-tape machine, with $\kappa = 2^{-182}$.
root.method: reduce exact multiplication to radix-digit convolution, compute that convolution with fast tape transforms, and check that the output is exact

motivation.text: The fixed-tape bound needs cheap address rearrangements and transform layers, so the argument replaces the costly steps by linear combinations of intermediate data.

quote.quote: The algorithm uses linear combinations of intermediate data to reduce the cost of both address rearrangement and Fourier-transform layers

children.claim: Exact multiplication reduces to a convolution of short integer coefficients obtained by splitting each input into radix digits.
children.method: split each input into radix digits and convolve

motivation.text: Short coefficients keep each convolution cheap, so the cost comes from the transforms rather than from the digits.

children.claim: Multiplication reduces to convolution of short integer coefficients.

quote.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients

children.claim: The Fourier transforms in the convolution are replaced by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.
children.method: resample Gaussian weights onto power-of-two axes

motivation.text: Power-of-two axis lengths let the later steps use butterfly layers and polynomial transforms.

children.claim: The Fourier transforms needed for the convolution become multidimensional transforms with power-of-two axes.

children.claim: One coordinate of the array is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r + 1$, with $r$ a power of two.
children.method: store one coordinate as polynomial coefficients and use powers of $y$ as roots of unity

motivation.text: Powers of y then serve as roots of unity, so multiplying by such a root is only a signed shift of the coefficient list.

children.claim: One coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r + 1$, with $r$ a power of two.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

children.claim: The transforms are synthetic polynomial transforms whose roots of unity are powers of the polynomial variable.
children.method: evaluate the transforms with polynomial roots of unity

motivation.text: Roots of unity that are powers of the variable cost only shifts and signs, so each transform reduces to address rearrangement and two-point butterflies.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits can be interchanged in time that grows more slowly than linearly in $u$.
children.method: build the permutation from XOR combinations of intermediate data in a linear network

motivation.text: A permutation of fields can be built from XOR combinations, which a linear network carries out while restoring its scratch values.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous address fields of $u$ bits are interchanged by the first procedure.

quote.quote: The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in an array

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two interchanged address fields.

children.claim: A butterfly layer on the selected bits of several axes is applied at once, in a single pass.
children.method: apply the layer to all selected bits together in one tape procedure

motivation.text: A single pass avoids the whole-array scans that separate butterfly factors would need.

quote.quote: whereas separate butterfly factors would require D whole-array passes

children.claim: The second procedure applies the two-point map on selected coordinate bits simultaneously.

children.claim: Each tape procedure is a fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values and restores its scratch values.
children.method: realise each procedure as a fixed linear network with frames on its wires

motivation.text: Frames on the wires let a pointwise gate act on arrays without disturbing their representation.

children.claim: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values.

quote.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values

children.claim: A linear network on three-element subsets exchanges two banks of values and restores its scratch wires.
children.method: label the triples by subspaces whose inclusions bound the change of frame

motivation.text: Orthogonality of the indicator vectors gives subspace assignments with the nesting that the change of frame needs.

children.claim: The number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s < Wm$, so each recursive level saves a power.
children.method: count the smaller calls against the wire count and the label dimension

motivation.text: A recursion whose branching factor is strictly below the growth of the rank saves a power at each level.

children.claim: The total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s < Wm$.

adds.meaning: The number of wires in the network.

adds.meaning: The number of coordinates of each vector in the label space.

children.claim: The radix-digit coefficients are placed on distinct prime cyclic axes by a map that preserves convolution.
children.method: relabel the coefficients by mixed-radix digits for the coprime axis lengths

motivation.text: Mixed-radix relabeling turns one cyclic convolution into a multidimensional one whose axis lengths are pairwise coprime.

children.claim: The radix-digit coefficient list is placed on prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution.

quote.quote: a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

children.claim: The source and target coordinate permutations stay inside the transform identity and are not executed as sorts.
children.method: keep both permutations in the transform formula

motivation.text: Keeping the permutations in the formula means they cancel across the convolution instead of being executed as separate sorts.

quote.quote: so they need not be executed as separate full sorts

children.claim: Section 8 retains the source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity.

children.claim: The middle transform, including its target permutation, becomes a normalized cyclic convolution.
children.method: rewrite the transform as a cyclic convolution multiplied by chirp factors

motivation.text: A chirp factorisation turns the middle transform into a cyclic convolution, which the earlier steps already compute.

children.claim: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into a cyclic convolution.

children.claim: A phase twist turns the last cyclic coordinate into a coordinate of a polynomial ring.
children.method: multiply the coefficients by roots of unity

motivation.text: The twist makes the wrap-around of the cyclic convolution match the negative wrap of the polynomial ring.

children.claim: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial coordinate.

quote.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate

children.claim: Convolution on the remaining axes over the polynomial ring is computed with synthetic transforms, a pointwise product, and packed integer products.
children.method: pack the coefficients into integers, multiply them, and unpack

motivation.text: Packing turns each polynomial product into an integer product that the established multiplier can compute.

children.claim: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product.

quote.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order

children.claim: The polynomial products use signed packing and the established multiplier as an ordinary subroutine.

quote.quote: Their polynomial products use signed packing and the established O(n log n) multiplier as an ordinary subroutine

children.claim: The recovered coefficient error is below one half, so rounding returns the exact integer coefficients.
children.method: bound the error accumulated through each stage

motivation.text: Once the total error is below one half, rounding to the nearest integer returns the true coefficient.

children.claim: The recovered coefficient error is strictly below one half.

quote.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below 1/2

children.claim: Carries across the radix digits turn the recovered coefficients into the exact binary product.
children.method: propagate carries through the coefficients in increasing order

motivation.text: Carry propagation converts the integer coefficient vector into a binary string with the same value.

children.claim: Carries are propagated to obtain the exact binary product.

quote.quote: propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product
